Article Title: 7 killed, several injured in stampede-like incident at Bihar's Lakhisarai temple
Article Text:
A stampede-like situation in Bihar temple, claims several lives.

Earlier incident in Muzaffarpur

NEW DELHI: Seven people were killed and several others injured in a stampede-like incident at Ashokdham Temple in Bihar’s Lakhisarai on early Monday, as news agency ANI quoted Bihar police.The incident took place as a large crowd had gathered at the temple, officials said.It also took place on Shravan’s Somvaar, a day that typically draws large numbers of devotees to Shiva temples.SDPO Shivam Kumar told ANI, "Seven casualties have been reported. It is being said that an electric pole fell there and people were electrocuted, which led to a stampede-like situation. We can tell you the exact reason only after verifying everything."Lakhisarai DM Shailendra Kumar said, "The crowd swelled in an unprecedented manner. Around 6.30-6.45 am, two trains came here that too added to the crowd. Arrangements were made as we had anticipated the crowd."Explaining how the incident unfolded, the DM said the sheer pressure of the crowd caused one side of the barricading to give way.“We then came to know that the barricading broke on one side due to the crowd, and people fell on each other.We rushed 10-15 people here immediately,” he added.The injured were shifted to local medical facilities for treatment. District administration officials and police personnel remained at the site to manage the crowd and prevent any further untoward incident.Further investigation into the incident is underway, with more details awaited.In a separate incident on August 12, a passenger bus travelling from Motihari towards Chhatarpur caught fire on the NH-27 Barji overbridge in Muzaffarpur around 12.45 am.Sub-Divisional Fire Officer of Motipur Amrita Kumari said the fire was caused by a short circuit. All 35 passengers were safely evacuated.
Article Summary: Stampede-like incident took place at Ashokdham Temple in Bihar's Lakhisarai. Incident took place on Shravan’s Somvaar, a day that typically draws large numbers of devotees to Shiva temples. It is being said that an electric pole fell there and people were electrocuted.

Article Title: Slugfest over Congress's P Chidambaram's 'dimagi Naxal' post
Article Text:
Kiren Rijiju said PM was not referring to the opposition after P Chidambaram's 'dimagi Naxal' post.

NEW DELHI: PM Modi's 'dimagi Naxal' remark on August 15 became the subject of a political slugfest Sunday, with Congress 's P Chidambaram saying he was "proud to be a dimagi Naxal" to which BJP replied that the ex-home minister's remark shows how UPA govt was run.Union minister Kiren Rijiju said the PM was not referring to the opposition. "Only following are Dimagi Naxals: 1. Who support Maoists and reject Indian Constitution. 2. Who stand with separatists & support Article 370. 4. Who want to cut chicken neck to separate North-East from India," he said on X. tnnCongress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera responded on X: "Brother Kiren Rijiju, get your counting right first, then we'll answer. After 1 and 2 comes 3, not 4."BJP ally TDP MP and former IPS officer Tenneti Krishna Prasad backed PM's "dimagi Naxals" remarks, saying a new form of "intellectual Naxalism" has emerged. "The forest Naxalites and Maoists have been removed from forests; now this new form has emerged. Therefore, we have to remain extremely vigilant and protect our country, especially our youth," he said in a video statement, according to news agency PTI.In an apparent reference to Rahul Gandhi, Tenneti Krishna said, "Today, forest Naxalites have gone, and a new form has emerged. I call them 'intellectual Naxalites'. They do not operate in forests; they operate in cities. They organise seminars in air-conditioned halls.BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad said Chidambaram "has become the face of the Congress ecosystem which nurtures Maoism". He recalled that as home minister, Chidambaram had expressed willingness to hold talks with Naxals when they had killed 76 security personnel, while JNU had witnessed an event lauding the killers. Under Modi govt, Maoism has not only been finished off but national flag is also flying in former strongholds of Maoists, he said.BJP also kept up its attack on Congress for allegedly insulting national song Vande Mataram, with BJP president Nitin Nabin, saying bowing to fundamentalist forces has become a permanent policy of Congress. Besides the attempt by Sonia Gandhi to "stop" the recital of Vande Mataram's full version at Congress headquarters, its govt in Kerala removed the song altogether from the Independence Day event, he said.
Article Summary: P Chidambaram said he was "proud to be a dimagi Naxal" to which BJP replied that the remark shows how UPA govt was run. Union minister Kiren Rijiju said the PM was not referring to the opposition. Bowing to fundamentalist forces has become a permanent policy of Congress.

Article Title: Never accepted Nalsar invitation, so no question of going: CJI
Article Text:
CJI Kant told TOI he 'never consented to Nalsar's invitation'.

NEW DELHI:Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has not accepted the invitation to be chief guest at the convocation of National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (Nalsar) University of Law amid a row sparked by a section of students opposing his presence at the event which snowballed after Bar Council of India jumped in and ordered blackballing of the graduates before retracting with regret.Hours after addressing VCs of national law universities at Jodhpur, CJI Kant told TOI he "never consented to Nalsar's invitation" to be chief guest at the convocation."The question of me attending the convocation does not arise," CJI said. Four days ago, Nalsar confirmed it had, in keeping with tradition, invited CJI Kant to be chief guest at the ceremony that is likely to be held at the end of Aug or in Sept.Of Nalsar's 1,400-odd students, more than 400 had opposed CJI Kant as chief guest, citing his remarks during a hearing on petitions related to the students' march to Parliament on July 20 and alleged police excesses.The CJI-led bench is seized of a bunch of petitions seeking independent inquiry into the alleged police excesses on students, use of pellet guns and facial recognition devices for profiling students in alleged breach of right to privacy.It has also accepted a petition by the relatives of injured police personnel seeking strict action against "criminal elements" who infiltrated the students' agitation and caused widespread violence and damage to public property while abusing PM and other constitutional functionaries.The students appeared to have taken umbrage at the CJI-led bench declining to take suo motu cognisance of the alleged police excesses against protesters when an advocate, without filing a proper petition, made the request on July 22, claiming he had video footage of the same. The CJI had asked him to file a proper petition articulating his allegations.However, when the advocate, without producing a scrap of a paper, persisted with his request that the bench watch the videos, the CJI, with a heavy cache of cases already before him, had asked him not to waste judicial time and suggested he file a proper petition.Petitions raising similar concerns were subsequently filed and entertained by the CJI-led bench, which had asked police not to take any coercive action against students and preserve all video and CCTV camera footage as well as sought suggestions for an independent inquiry into the incident and setting up a commission to lay down pan-India guidelines for graded action by police to control protests turning violent.The controversy over students' opposition to the invite to CJI snowballed after BCI chairperson, Manan Kumar Mishra, unilaterally issued a letter to the Nalsar vice-chancellor seeking an inquiry and identification of students who opposed the CJI's presence at the convocation and threatened to debar them from getting registered as advocates.Faced with condemnation, BCI quickly withdrew the circular. SC has sought its response while observing that the regulator had no business wading into a matter which concerned CJI and Nalsar students.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has not accepted the invitation to be chief guest at the convocation of National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (Nalsar) University of Law. The row sparked by a section of students opposing his presence at the event snowballed after Bar Council of India jumped in and ordered blackballing of graduates.

Article Title: Fleeing drowning scene not proof of culpability, says SC; acquits 2 held guilty of killing friend
Article Text:
An SC bench said the evidence for an accidental drowning was more plausible than homicide.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Observing that the human mind can sometimes act foolishly, especially in the face of unpredictable adversity, Supreme Court has said that such behaviour cannot be the sole basis of conviction and acquitted two men who had been held guilty of killing their friend.They were convicted by trial court and high court because their friend drowned in a river in their presence and instead of trying to rescue him, they left the spot and went to watch a movie, actions which were held as evidence of their culpability.Gujarat high court held that their behaviour was proof that they had killed the friend, and it was not a case of drowning in the river, sentencing them to life imprisonment.Setting aside the order of trial court and high court, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there was no evidence to prove that it was a case of murder and held that the deceased had drowned accidentally."The accused are guilty of having fled from the spot and not having attempted to rescue the drowning person by crying out for help. Their conduct of having gone for a movie after witnessing their friend drowning, though reprehensible, cannot be found to be an incriminating circumstance, to establish murder rather than drowning. The hypothesis of innocence is crystal clear, and circumstances indicate an accident and not a premeditated murder," the bench said.Disagreeing with the findings of the HC, the bench said, "We also have to notice the high court's presumption that no person who saw his friend drowning would go to a movie or would take the trouble of bringing back empty soda bottles to the shop from where they purchased it. If such a presumption is accepted then it can be presumed that even after a premeditated murder, the accused would not conduct themselves in that manner. ""The human mind, as has often been held by this court, is at the same time fickle, manipulative and imaginative and the actions, the result of a deprived or a foolish mindset, especially in the face of adversities, cannot be predicted. The subsequent conduct on which the high court found possible the prosecution story of murder rather than of drowning, in this case we are unable to accept. It is the hypothesis of an accidental drowning that looms large from the evidence led at the trial; more plausible than a homicide," SC said.Challenging their conviction, the accused submitted that they, at worst, could be held guilty of a misadventure which turned fatal for their friend, and there was absolutely no evidence to prove even a homicidal death. They, however, admitted that they fled the scene in panic.
Article Summary: Supreme Court acquits two men who had been held guilty of killing their friend. They were convicted because their friend drowned in a river in their presence and instead of trying to rescue him, they left the spot and went to watch a movie. Supreme Court said the evidence for an accidental drowning was more plausible than homicide.

Article Title: ED: TMC paid little-known company Rs 160 crore to buy a jet & helicopter
Article Text:
ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company.

NEW DELHI: An ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company has found that the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress allegedly funded Rs 160 crore from the party's coffers to a little-known firm, Carewell Aviation India Pvt Ltd, to buy an Embraer jet and an Agusta VIP helicopter, which it subsequently rented out to TMC for Rs 187 crore.Sources said the money laundering probe was focused on TMC providing an interest-free security deposit of Rs 88.5 crore to the aviation company, which had no funds to buy the jet and the chopper it then gave to the party on rent. As soon as it received the security deposit, Carewell Aviation transferred it to its offshore entity, Carewell Flyjet IFSC Pvt Ltd, registered in Gujarat's Gift City, treated as foreign territory, for further purchase of the jet and the helicopter.Another fund transfer of over Rs 16 crore from Cayman Island and related to the deal is under investigation.TMC was required to pay Rs 186.9 crore, exclusive of GST, for using the jet over 72 months and the chopper for 56 months. Although it did not fully utilise the minimum guaranteed flying hours under the charter agreement, the party went on to hire aircraft and helicopters from other companies during this period (2021-26) for a sum of Rs 149 crore, sources said.When contacted, a TMC source said, "Since the matter is sub judice, we do not want to comment."The "suspicious" nature of transactions has led ED to delve into the issue of why TMC paid an interest-free security deposit of Rs 88.5 crore when it had to pay charges for renting the aircraft and helicopter. The agreement provided that TMC pay a minimum monthly charge of Rs 90 lakh for the aircraft and Rs 60 lakh for the helicopter.Carewell Aviation came into being only a few months after TMC returned to office for the third time after the April 2021 assembly elections. Then, after losing the assembly polls in 2026, TMC paid three months advance rental to the company to cover the period till Sept 2026: something that the agency says is contrary to the norm.Sources said ED has questioned directors of Carewell Aviation over these transactions and recorded their statements on issues such as why it charged TMC Rs 16.5 lakh per flying hour for the jet and when it billed others, who had not helped it with something as crucial as a security deposit, a much lower amount of Rs 7.6 lakh per hour for flying Embraer.Investigations also showed, sources said, that TMC paid Rs 75 lakh per flying hour to another charter service, Windborne Aviation, for hiring a Falcon 2000 aircraft. TMC used the Falcon aircraft for only about 11-12 flying hours but paid Rs 9.1 crore, which was roughly Rs 75.7 lakh per flying hour.According to sources, the money trail showed that over Rs 160 crore was transferred to Carewell Aviation and its group entities between July 2021 and June 2026 for "charter services" for the Embraer aircraft and the Agusta chopper. Investigators suspect the transaction to be an "artificial commercial arrangement" and a "calculated device", bereft of any genuine actual financial rationale, considering that the two aircraft were allegedly purchased entirely out of the corpus received from TMC, and the two aviation assets were rented back to the party.The jet was purchased two months after the charter agreement was signed and security deposit provided. Similarly, the charter agreement for the VIP helicopter was signed by TMC in March 2025 while the chopper was purchased a month later in April.Carewell Aviation, which was incorporated on Sept 14, 2021, with Pawan Jaju and Ramesh Jaju as its directors, purchased the Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft on June 6, 2023, and the Agusta 109 Grand helicopter on April 17, 2025, using its offshore entity.
Article Summary: ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company. Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress allegedly funded Rs 160 crore to a little-known firm. Carewell Aviation India Pvt Ltd bought an Embraer jet and an Agusta VIP helicopter, which it subsequently rented out to TMC.

Article Title: E coli found in drinking water, rail stations lack basic facilities: CAG
Article Text:
Water samples were found to contain coliform bacteria.

NEW DELHI: Comptroller and Auditor General has flagged gaps in sanitation and minimum essential amenities at 458 out of 512 railway stations, including presence of E coli bacteria in water coolers at eight stations.The CAG report on "passenger amenities and sanitation at non-suburban railway stations", presented in Parliament last week, said bacteriological analysis of drinking water was not carried out at 59 stations in six zones."Water sample from water coolers was positive for E coli at two stations (Coimbatore and Palakkad junctions) in Southern Railway, one station (Hyderabad) in South Central Railway, four stations (Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Bhiwandi Road, Kalyan and Lonavala) in Central Railway, and one station (Madhupur) in Eastern Railway," the report said.It said the results of drinking water samples collected from taps at 49 stations in eight zones during 2022-23 and 56 stations in nine zones during 2023-24 indicated presence of coliforms bacteria.Following the CAG report, railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and top officials held a review meeting. In a statement, Railways said a new "Tank to Tap" water filtration system will be implemented at 20,000 locations. It said water tanks would be replaced and regular water testing carried out at source and outlet points.There will be centralised monitoring and accountability, and scheduled cleaning and maintenance of storage tanks.CAG also said 458 out of 512 selected stations were deficient in provision of minimum essential amenities. It found stations like CSMT, Howrah, Sealdah, New Delhi and Mumbai Central deficient in seating arrangements, sanitary facilities, dustbins and electronic train indicator boards, among others.The report, after analysing Passenger Amenities Management System, found deficiencies in provision of amenities against norms, such as shortfall of toilets at 201 stations, urinals at 403 stations, and water taps at 2,035 stations, among others.
Article Summary: Bacteriological analysis of drinking water was not carried out at 59 stations in six zones. Water sample from water coolers was positive for E coli at two stations. Railways said a new "Tank to Tap" water filtration system will be implemented at 20,000 locations.

Article Title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
Article Text:
SC gave the government two weeks to take a final call on introducing warning labels for packaged foods.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday sharply criticised the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India FSSAI ) over the delay in introducing front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, warning that it would issue directions if the government failed to take a final decision.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record, making it clear that the government could either implement the proposed warning labels on its own or face judicial intervention."This is your last chance. Next time we will dictate the judgment," the bench said, according to ANI.The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children and questioned the government's reluctance to move ahead with stronger nutritional warnings."Why? You don't want people of this country to remain healthy? More particularly growing children?" the bench asked during the hearing.Appearing for the Centre, additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar argued that applying strict warning standards could create complications for traditional Indian food items. He said products such as namkeen could end up carrying red warning symbols because of their fat or salt content.He also argued that international nutritional standards might not be directly applicable to Indian dietary habits, pointing out that even two eggs could exceed the prescribed daily fat limit.The court, however, was unconvinced.The bench said consumers were already aware that packaged foods contained sugar, fat and carbohydrates, but front-of-pack warning labels would provide a simpler and more effective way of communicating nutritional risks before a purchase was made.The judges also rejected the argument that warning labels could adversely affect manufacturers.According to ANI, the bench observed that the final decision to purchase a product would continue to rest with consumers and that commercial considerations could not take precedence over public health.During the proceedings, senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for a manufacturer, attempted to make submissions. The court responded by stating that the case concerned the health of citizens and that manufacturers could not determine government policy on the issue.Senior advocate Devadutt Kamat suggested that food products could be categorised differently and that detailed nutritional information should be displayed.The bench clarified that it was not opposed to any particular food product but was only seeking greater consumer awareness."In this country, how many people can afford dry fruits? And how many children buy Kurkure? That makes all the difference. We are not against any particular product. We only want the person purchasing it to know what he is consuming," the court said, according to ANI.The bench also referred to its February 10, 2026, order, in which it had previously addressed the issue and laid down its observations.During Thursday's hearing, the petitioner's counsel drew the court's attention to the minutes of an FSSAI meeting held on March 7, which allegedly reflected a position contrary to the suggestions made by the court earlier.The judges also took exception to the Centre's argument that India could not easily adopt international standards relating to nutritional warnings."We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it's not possible to match the international standards, more particularly developed countries. Should India remain an undeveloped country?" the bench asked, according to ANI."The world should know that India is concerned about the health of its citizens and more particularly children," it added.The case stems from a petition seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat.The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products before buying them.The issue has also been discussed by Parliament's Committee on Subordinate Legislation, headed by Shiv Sena Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora, who has advocated studying Singapore's Nutri-Grade model as a possible template for India.Separately, the Union health ministry has proposed displaying "sugar and oil boards" in schools, offices and other public institutions as part of a broader effort to encourage healthier eating habits and reduce excessive consumption of sugar and oil.
Article Summary: Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record. The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children. The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products.

Article Title: Harsimrat Kaur Badal 'deeply touched' by PM Modi's 'kind gesture' after attack on Sukhbir Badal

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal on Friday said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief, Sukhbir Singh Badal , who was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.This marked the Badal family's first reaction to the attack on the former Punjab deputy chief minister."Truly grateful, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, for your personal call to inquire about Sardar Sukhbir Singh Badal ji’s health and for your good wishes for his speedy recovery following the dastardly attack on him inside a Gurudwara Sahib in Nanded, Maharashtra," Harsimrat Badal, SAD's only Lok Sabha MP, wrote on X.She also thanked the prime minister for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with the state police in the probe."Your concern, support and wishes during this difficult time mean a lot to all of us in the family, our party and to the people of Punjab. I am deeply touched by your kind gesture. I am also grateful to you for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with Maharashtra Police in the probe," the Bathinda MP added.On Thursday, Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked by a kirpan-wielding assailant while leaving the Mata Sahib Devaji Gurdwara at Mudkhed in Maharashtra’s Nanded district. The assailant was arrested at the spot.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered an inquiry into the attack and spoke to Sukhbir Singh Badal over the phone. The SAD president is learnt to have told Fadnavis that he was stable, ANI reported.Earlier, Badal was also targeted in an attempted shooting at the Golden Temple in Amritsar in December 2024 while he was performing “seva”. The attacker allegedly tried to fire at him but was overpowered before he could cause any harm.The 2024 attack took place while Badal was carrying out “seva” after the Akal Takht, the highest temporal authority in Sikhism, declared him a “tankhaiya,” or guilty of religious misconduct, over decisions taken by the SAD-led Punjab government between 2007 and 2017.The SAD and BJP, which currently lead the governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, are former allies. In 2020, the SAD ended its alliance with the BJP in protest against the Centre’s contentious farm laws, which were later withdrawn.Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week, triggering speculation that the former allies could reunite ahead of the Punjab assembly elections early next year.
Article Summary: Harsimrat Kaur Badal said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief. Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed “strong disapproval” of the Bar Council of India’s (BCI) now-revoked order barring the enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad’s NALSAR University of Law as advocates after a section of students objected to the university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony.Kant, heading a bench also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said students have a right to protest peacefully and described the episode as a “dialogue” between him and the students."If students are protesting peacefully, who is BCI to take action? It is the right of the students to protest peacefully. It is a dialogue between students and me. No one else has to step in," the CJI said.Expressing its strong disapproval, the Supreme Court also stayed any coercive action against students or faculty by BCI or state Councils."It (the letter) was absolutely uncalled for," the bench added.The bench posted the matter for hearing after two weeks.On Thursday, the BCI had directed all state bar councils not to enrol any 2026 graduate of NALSAR University of Law as an advocate until further orders. It withdrew the directive within hours following an uproar on social media.In its initial statement, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra said the council was examining allegations regarding a campaign against CJI Kant’s participation in the university’s convocation and had sought a report identifying those responsible.The BCI later modified its decision and allowed state bar councils to enrol the university’s 2026 graduates as advocates before withdrawing the notification altogether.The revised notification stated that the “vast majority” of students were innocent and should not be made to suffer for the alleged “misconduct” of a few.Around 450 graduating students of NALSAR had urged the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant as chief guest, citing his alleged refusal to hear pleas concerning “police brutality” against students who had marched to Parliament on July 20 seeking the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG question paper leak in May. Pradhan’s resignation on July 25 brought the protests to an end.
Article Summary: Supreme Court expresses "strong disapproval" of Bar Council of India's now- revoked order. BCI had barred enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law as advocates. Students objected to university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony.

Article Title: Phuket plunge: Airbus sends initial report to AI, seeks maintenance details
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: “The elevators (control up and down movement of aircraft) and ailerons (controls left and right movement) surfaces were lost for around four seconds.” Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.“Based on analysis of the DFDR (digital flight data recorder),” Airbus found that within seven seconds between 9:32:44 am and 9:32:51 am, there was a loss of hydraulics systems — pressurised fluids which enable flight controls to move. At this point, the autopilot was disconnected and the aircraft’s nose went up (increase in pitch). All timings are in IST.The Airbus preliminary communication sent to AI on Aug 10 says “at (9:32:46 am) auto pilot 2 was disconnected, and full nose down (pitch down) input began being applied on first officer side with no direct response from the flight control surfaces” due to the loss of hydraulics. Five seconds later, a single hydraulic system was recovered and a few seconds later the remaining two systems were back, leading to recovery of normal flight control.Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities as it continues its event assessment. “Since load exceedances were detected during the sudden altitude change, (maintenance) inspections must be performed.Please provide the inspection results once they are completed. Please provide more detailed pilot reports from the reported event clarifying what it is observed during the event,” the communication says.“...this event requires an analysis considering both aircraft systems and structural integrity, as airframe may have been affected by the movement,” it adds.While probe is on by Airbus and France’s accident investigator under the ambit of India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, several pilots are questioning why Air India decided to fly the aircraft all the way to Delhi after it had recovered from the technical events.
Article Summary: Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities. Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.

Article Title: Park outside your Bengaluru home? It may soon cost up to Rs 25,000 a year
Article Text:
Bengaluru plans to introduce paid annual permits for on-street residential parking (File photo enhanced with AI)

Rules propose

Private operators to enforce rules

Common parking portal planned

Penalties prescribed

Illegal parking on roads

Rs 500 for cars

Rs 300 for two-wheelers

Parking on footpaths

Rs 1,000 for cars

Rs 600 for two-wheelers

Key conditions

Residential street parking allowed only through permit

Permit valid for one year

Parking outside the permitted area will be treated as a violation





BENGALURU: The city is all set to put a price on one of its most contested public resources, road space.Under the proposed Greater Bengaluru Authority Parking Rules, 2026, residents who want to park their cars on the road outside their homes will have to obtain annual permits, with fees varying by vehicle type.The draft also proposes sweeping restrictions on where vehicles can be parked, particularly around major roads and Metro stations.There are proposals for a complete ban on parking on arterial roads identified as high-density corridors by Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).It also seeks parking restrictions during peak hours on select arterial roads notified by traffic police.In addition, vehicles would not be allowed to park near junctions, bus stops, transit hubs, pedestrian crossings and footpaths, with detailed setback requirements prescribed under the rules.The proposed rules seek to significantly reduce on-street parking near public transport hubs.Initially, on-street parking would be prohibited within 150 metres of Metro and suburban railway station boundaries. The draft allows city corporations to gradually increase the no-parking zone up to 500 metres.The proposal is expected to impact several high-footfall Metro station areas across the city where commuters currently rely on adjoining roads for parking.In a shift from the current system, the draft proposes to authorise private operators managing public parking facilities to issue violation notices, collect parking-related charges, tow vehicles and clamp vehicles after being formally authorised by city corporations.The operators would be required to record video evidence of violations before towing vehicles, and all towing activities would be overseen by traffic police.To increase organised parking supply, the draft allows city corporations to lease vacant private plots and develop them into public parking facilities.Private landowners who voluntarily convert vacant plots into parking facilities would be eligible for incentives, including property tax exemptions.Owners providing mechanised or multi-level parking facilities could receive 100% exemption from property tax and service charges, while owners offering surface-level parking could receive a 50% exemption.The draft directs Metro, BMTC and suburban rail agencies to create off-street parking facilities on land available with them, particularly at interchange stations and peripheral locations, to encourage park-and-ride travel.Transit agencies may also offer discounted parking rates for commuters using public transport.All parking operators, city corporations and transit agencies would be required to share real-time information on parking availability, occupancy and pricing with GBA.The data would eventually be integrated into a common citywide parking portal and mobile application to help motorists locate available parking spaces and enable authorities to plan future parking infrastructure.Traffic police will continue to have powers to enforce no-parking regulations, tow vehicles and take action against repeat offenders.The draft also allows city corporations to increase parking rates based on demand and location and proposes higher charges for longer parking durations to discourage all-day occupation of valuable road space.
Article Summary: Bengaluru plans to introduce paid annual permits for on-street residential parking. Residents will have to obtain annual permits, with fees varying by vehicle type. The draft also proposes sweeping restrictions on where vehicles can be parked, particularly around major roads and Metro stations.

NEW DELHI: After earlier uncertainty, there are now clear indications that barrierless tolling on national highway (NH) stretches, coupled with e-notices for violations, is inculcating greater discipline among road users.At Choryasi toll plaza on NH-48 in Gujarat, the first to go live, e-notices fell from 1.7 lakh in May to 1.1 lakh in June and further to 92,240 in July. Mundka toll plaza in Delhi, which went live on May 10, recorded 1.69 lakh e-notices in June, with a marginal decline to 1.67 lakh in July.Multilane free flow (MLFF), or barrierless tolling, is currently operational at five toll plazas. It was rolled out at Daulatpura on Delhi-Jaipur highway and Gharaunda on Delhi-Chandigarh highway in the third and fourth week of June, respectively. Manoharpura on Delhi-Jaipur highway was the latest to go live, on July 1.Data show that e-notices issued during the first month of MLFF operations at Daulatpura, Gharaunda and Manoharpura were significantly lower than those issued when the system was launched at Choryasi and Mundka. Daulatpura issued 33,038 e-notices in July, while Gharaunda and Manoharpura recorded 86,760 and 70,550, respectively.“As awareness about e-notices for toll non-payment spreads, road users are becoming more compliant. A large number of vehicle owners, particularly car users without active FASTags, are also falling in line,” said an official involved in NHAI’s tolling system.Failure to pay or challenge an e-notice within 72 hours can result in the vehicle owner being liable to pay double the toll. Prolonged non-payment can also affect access to Vahan-related services.

Article Title: How PM Modi has changed focus of Independence Day speeches
Article Text:
As the country has progressed, so has the theme of PM Modi’s speeches.

In all 13 speeches, PM Modi focused on taking the country forward.

NEW DELHI: From access to aspiration and from problems to potential - the focus of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day speeches has kept changing since 2014.Those tracking his speeches over the last 12 years have noted how in the initial year, Prime Minister Modi focused on issues such as toilets, bank accounts, poverty and fertiliser shortages. That has given way to attention to priorities like 6G, semiconductor, AI and quantum computing.If 2014 had mention of toilets as a challenge, Saturday he renewed his pitch for women's reservation in legislature. "In the early years of Modi govt, the speeches were often about problems that we may today consider ordinary. But PM's tone was urgent when he addressed them. The challenge was to fix what was broken, reach those who had been left out," said an official.As the country has progressed, so has the theme of his speeches, with a constant nudge to move to the next level, while setting the bar high, officials said.In all his 13 speeches so far, the pitch has always been on taking the country forward and ensuring everyone in society benefits from the gains and the schemes."Over the years, his vocabulary began to change. The conversation moved from plugging gaps to building capabilities, from solving immediate problems to creating systems that could prevent those problems from defining India again," the official added.In 2014, Prime Minister Modi called for eradicating poverty. Over the years, the focus has shifted to building a developed nation as poverty levels fell and crores moved out of extreme poverty.So, in Prime Minister Modi's 2026 speech, he underlined how social security cover has seen a four-fold jump to 100 crore citizens in the last 12 years.Women have remained a prominent theme over the past 12 years.If in 2014 he highlighted the plight of women who had to wait for sunset to venture out to ease themselves in the open since they did not have access to toilets, by 2018, the attention had moved to permanent commission for women in the armed forces.And, in his latest speech, PM Modi underlined the need for 33% reservation for women in legislatures, for which he sought the opposition's support.The shift is also visible in the focus on farmers - from preventing farmer suicides to tapping global markets through FTAs.
Article Summary: In all 13 speeches, PM Modi focused on taking the country forward. As the country has progressed, so has the theme of his speeches. In 2014, Prime Minister Modi called for eradicating poverty. Over the years, the focus has shifted to building a developed nation.

Article Title: NTA admits errors, orders fresh NET for 3 subjects
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: National Testing Agency (NTA) on Sunday acknowledged that the UGC-NET papers in English, Commerce and Sociology had multiple errors and repeated questions, and said the defects were too extensive to be addressed simply by dropping questions after the answer-key challenge process. It has ordered fresh examinations for all three subjects.The re-tests will be held on September 9 and 10. English will be conducted from 9am to noon on September 9, Commerce from 3pm to 6pm the same day, and Sociology from 9am to noon on September 10. No additional examination fee will be charged.The decision came hours after NTA released provisional answer keys for 84 of the 87 UGC-NET subjects but withheld the keys for these three papers, nearly seven weeks after the June examination.NTA said a committee set up after receiving “several complaints” found “many factual, typographical, translation errors”, including misspelt names of prominent scholars, garbled book titles, wrongly worded questions, grammatical and punctuation mistakes and non-standard terms used for established concepts. The committee also found repetition of a “significant number” of questions previously asked.The agency said papers carrying defects of this extent did not meet the standards of a fair and error-free examination and that the problems could not be corrected merely by dropping questions after challenges were received.TOI had on July 1 reported complaints over the Sociology and English papers. Sociology candidates alleged that the June 30 paper contained spelling and grammatical errors, mangled names of well-known thinkers, poor Hindi translations and questions apparently unrelated to the prescribed syllabus. Some also alleged that parts of the paper appeared AI-generated.Candidates had pointed out that “Ritzer” appeared as “Putzer”, “Parsons” as “Parsow”, “Ghurye” as “Ghunye” and A R Desai as “A K Desai”, among several other errors.The English paper had also come under scrutiny after candidates alleged that 67 of its 150 questions were identical to questions asked in the 2024 examination, with even the sequence of answer options reportedly unchanged. Complaints over repetition were subsequently raised in Commerce as well.The episode comes two years after the June 2024 UGC-NET was cancelled a day after it was held following inputs received by UGC from the National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit under the home ministry indicating that the integrity of the examination may have been compromised. The test was subsequently conducted afresh.The current re-examination will, however, not hold up results in the other 84 subjects. NTA said their results would be declared as scheduled and JRF allocation and certificates for Assistant Professor and PhD eligibility would not be delayed.For assistant professor eligibility, NTA said the number qualifying would be 6% of candidates who appeared in the June test or the re-test, whichever is higher.
Article Summary: National Testing Agency says papers in English, Commerce and Sociology had multiple errors and repeated questions. NTA says defects were too extensive to be addressed simply by dropping questions after the answer-key challenge process. It has ordered fresh examinations for all three subjects on September 9 and 10.

Article Title: Beyond bloodline: How donated milk is saving India’s most vulnerable newborns
Article Text:
Doctors strongly challenge the widespread belief that most mothers simply do not produce enough milk.

When a mother is not there

The babies for whom every feed matters

The mother who gives

How does a mother donate?

Medical journey before reaching baby

Why informal sharing is not the same thing

More needy babies than donor mothers

Small act with enormous human meaning

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The first thing a mother wants to do after bringing a baby into the world is often the simplest: hold the child close and feed it. But for some newborns, that first feed never comes.Their mothers may be critically ill, separated from them, unable to breastfeed immediately or, in the most heartbreaking cases, no longer alive.For a premature baby weighing just a few hundred grams, however, waiting for circumstances to change is not always an option.This is where another mother can step in.Human milk banks in India are built around a quiet act of generosity: a lactating mother donates milk her own baby does not need, and through a carefully regulated medical system, that milk reaches a newborn whose own mother cannot provide it."Milk bank helps one mother save the baby of another mother," said Dr Poonam Sidana, director of neonatology and paediatrics at CK Birla Hospital, Delhi.The idea may sound straightforward. But behind every bottle is a mother who has agreed to share something deeply personal and another family placing its trust in a system to provide their fragile newborn with the safest possible nourishment.Dr Satish Tiwari, founder and convener of the Human Milk Banking Association of India and professor of paediatrics, has spent decades trying to expand that system.He traces the movement in India to 1989, when the first human milk bank in India and Asia was established at Sion Hospital in Mumbai by Dr Armida Fernandes.By the mid-1990s, Tiwari had begun exploring milk banking while working on maternal and child nutrition and malnutrition."What we realised was that milk banks are needed not only in Mumbai or Surat or Udaipur, but it is a requirement all over India," he said.The babies who need donor human milk, he explained, are often those who have been separated from their mothers for reasons beyond anyone's control.A newborn may be admitted to a NICU at 500g or 700g, born at seven or eight months of gestation and too weak to breastfeed. The mother may have to return home while the baby remains in hospital."Mother may not be available for months when he is admitted in a neonatal care unit," Tiwari said.Then there are babies whose mothers have died."There may be the death of the mother. So the mother herself is not available for the baby," he said.There are also abandoned newborns and babies whose mothers are temporarily unable to breastfeed.In such situations, the conventional fallback has often been formula or other substitutes. But for a vulnerable premature baby, doctors say human milk can make an important difference."If you feed on mother's milk, which is through the milk bank, then the child's improvement or the child's outcome as far as his life is concerned becomes much, much better," Tiwari said.For premature and low-birth-weight infants, the issue is not simply about calories.Their digestive and immune systems are still developing, making them especially vulnerable to infections and serious complications.Sidana said the strongest evidence for donor human milk is in premature and low-birth-weight infants, particularly in reducing the incidence of necrotising enterocolitis, or NEC, a severe condition that can damage the intestine and, in serious cases, lead to infection and death."Donor human milk is believed to bring down the incidence of necrotising enterocolitis and some infections more than formula does in premature babies," she said.Human milk also contains bioactive and immune components that formula cannot replicate.But Sidana is clear about the hierarchy: when a mother can breastfeed her own baby, that remains the ideal."A mother's own milk, preferably via breastfeeding, is the best option since it is optimal for her infant and has the required nutrients and immunity that facilitate his or her growth and resistance to infections," she said.Donor human milk becomes the next option when that first choice is temporarily or permanently unavailable.Dr Sakshi Goel, senior consultant in obstetrics and gynaecology at Madhukar Rainbow Children's Hospital, Delhi, described it as a "transitional or supplemental resource" for newborns at risk."It should not take away from the importance of establishing and continuing with lactation," she said.That distinction is important because milk banks do not exist simply to distribute milk. They also help mothers breastfeed and, when possible, produce enough milk for their own babies.Tiwari strongly challenges the widespread belief that most mothers simply do not produce enough milk."The concept that mother is not able to make enough milk, basically we feel it is a misconception," he said.In most cases, he explained, breastfeeding is a physiological process. Difficulties can arise because of delayed initiation, poor positioning, inadequate feeding or the early introduction of formula or bottle feeding."If we start top milk or powder milk, then the mother's milk, it goes on decreasing," he said.That is why milk banks and lactation centres first try to understand why a mother believes she does not have enough milk."If there is some fault, we try to manage that fault in the feeding," Tiwari said. "And then we convince the mother that she has more milk as compared to the requirement of her child."Only when a mother has enough milk for her own baby does the conversation turn to donation."She cannot only feed her child, but she can also donate the milk," he said.For many mothers, that can become an unexpectedly emotional decision.They are not donating something abstract. They are expressing, collecting and handing over milk their bodies produced to nourish their own child.But in a regulated system, they know where it is going: to a newborn who needs it.The process begins not with a bottle, but with a conversation.Goel said a mother who wants to donate should approach a reputable human milk bank or Comprehensive Lactation Management Centre rather than trying to donate informally.The centre counsels her, reviews her medical history and determines whether she is eligible."After that, the mother goes through the essential screening and testing and is given instructions on how to express, collect and store her milk," Goel said.The milk is then collected through the recognised channel and subjected to the necessary processing and safety checks.Tiwari said milk banks initially relied heavily on mothers delivering in the same hospital. But awareness has slowly widened the donor pool."Now we have that type of mother also," he said of women who hear about milk banks and voluntarily approach them.Some centres have even begun using milk collection vans to travel between hospitals and homes.There is no commercial transaction involved."There is no monetary benefit to the mother who is donating," Tiwari said. "Similarly, we do not charge any mother for getting milk also.""Neither we give money or monetary benefit to the donor nor to the recipient. It is totally voluntary."That word — voluntary — is central to the idea. A mother is never expected to compromise her own baby's nourishment. She gives only what is surplus.The emotional generosity of donation is matched by a rigorous safety system.Donors are screened for communicable diseases and other health risks. Their medications are reviewed, as are lifestyle factors that could make the milk unsafe."We take three or four precautions," Tiwari said.Mothers are screened for illnesses such as hepatitis B and C and other infections that could potentially be transmitted to a recipient. They are also assessed for medicines that could harm a baby."If she is on some psychotropic drugs or some anti-cancer drugs or if she is on some habit-forming drugs, then we have to take care of that also," he said.Smoking and alcohol consumption are also considered."All these factors are considered, and screening is completed before collecting the mother's milk," he said.The donated milk then goes through processing and testing.According to Sidana, India's standards include Holder pasteurisation, in which milk is heated to 62.5°C for 30 minutes and then rapidly cooled.Samples undergo microbiological testing, and pasteurised milk is released only when cultures do not show bacterial growth.Pasteurisation does mean that donor human milk is not biologically identical to fresh mother's milk."Pasteurization processes modify various parts of human milk, especially a number of heat-sensitive enzymes and immune factors," Sidana said.But, she added, it preserves the nutritional composition and many of the biological qualities of human milk while significantly improving safety.For a highly vulnerable premature baby, that balance matters.The instinct to help another mother can be powerful enough to encourage direct sharing through friends, social networks or online groups.But doctors caution against confusing generosity with safety."A regulated milk bank is run in accordance with a proper medical and quality-control system," Sidana said.There is donor screening, testing, pasteurisation, storage and traceability.With informal sharing, those safeguards may disappear."There might be doubts about the health condition of the donor, medications that were taken, how the milk was stored, and whether it comes from the right source or is contaminated," Sidana said.The warning is particularly important for premature and sick newborns whose immune systems are already fragile."The problem does not lie in people who generously donate the milk," she said. "There is a problem of the lack of screening, control over the sources, storage practices, and testing for milk intended for very vulnerable neonates."The need for donor human milk can be greater than the available supply.Tiwari said many milk banks are still unable to meet the complete requirements of the hospitals where they operate.Goel said there is no reliable real-time evidence pointing to a single nationwide shortage because availability differs considerably between hospitals and regions. But demand can exceed local supply, especially where large numbers of premature or medically fragile newborns are being treated.When that happens, the most vulnerable babies are prioritised."The main point is fair allocation of resources while at the same time helping mothers with the establishment and maintenance of their own milk supply," Goel said.This is one reason awareness matters so much.At JIPMER, a July 2025 PIB release noted that the Amudham Thaipaal Maiyam's average voluntary milk collection had grown from about 400ml a day in its early years to around 1,000ml a day, with at least 20 babies, particularly premature infants, benefiting every day.But Tiwari believes India still has a long way to go.He said his association reaches doctors, medical students and hospitals through conferences, talks and awareness campaigns. NGOs and organisations such as Rotary have also helped with equipment, infrastructure and publicity."We are doing publicity on media. We are doing mouth-to-mouth publicity by the mother who has received the milk for her baby," he said.Human milk banking is ultimately a story about mothers.One mother may be sitting beside her own healthy baby, expressing milk her child does not immediately need.In another ward, another mother may be sitting beside an incubator, watching a tiny chest rise and fall and wondering whether her baby will make it through the night.Tiwari's message is simple."Mother's milk is best for any newborn child," he said.And for mothers who have more milk than their own babies need, he wants hesitation to give way to awareness."Most of the mothers, they have more milk as compared to the requirement of her child," he said. "Mother or the relatives or the grandparent, they should not hesitate in donating the milk."There is no grand ceremony when a bottle of donor milk leaves a milk bank.It is labelled, tested, pasteurised, stored and eventually carried to a NICU.But inside that bottle is something much larger than milk.It is the generosity of one mother reaching a baby she may never see.And for a newborn who has arrived too soon, whose mother is too ill, or who has lost the person who was meant to feed them, that generosity can become a lifeline.
Article Summary: Human milk banks in India are built around a quiet act of generosity. A lactating mother donates milk her own baby does not need, and through a carefully regulated medical system, that milk reaches a newborn whose own mother cannot provide it. Doctors strongly challenge the widespread belief that most mothers simply do not produce enough milk.

Article Title: Parliament at a standstill, protests on streets: The Monsoon session story
Article Text:
19% in Lok Sabha, 39% in Rajya Sabha: How Monsoon Session unfolded beyond the Parliament

Parliament sees low productivity

'Not a good session in terms of discussion'

Bills passed in Parliament

Bills passed by both the Houses

Bills passed in this Monsoon Session

The session began with a protest

From Pradhan to Shah

Rahul Gandhi trains guns at Amit Shah

The debate that moved between the House and outside

Monsoon Session

Jharkhand adds another layer

Pradhan calls Rahul Gandhi a 'habitual liar'

Then came the Ram Mandir protest

A Parliament that worked, but talked less

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For 25 days, Parliament’s Monsoon Session played out on two different stages.Inside the Houses, proceedings were repeatedly disrupted, adjournments were frequent and Question Hour had barely any time remaining. Outside, political activity rarely stopped. Students marched, opposition leaders protested, ministers traded charges, and the Parliament complex itself became a stage for demonstrations and symbolic political performances.Held from July 20 to August 13, the session produced an unusual contrast: legislation moved forward, but much of the political confrontation surrounding it played out beyond the floor of the two Houses.The numbers underline that contrast. Lok Sabha functioned for approximately 19% of its scheduled time, while Rajya Sabha functioned for around 39%. Question Hour was particularly badly hit, with less than 1% of its scheduled time utilised. The session had 19 sittings spread over 25 days.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju acknowledged the distinction between legislative output and debate.“It was a good session…we have passed 13 bills; but it was not a good session in terms of discussion,” he said, while accusing the opposition of avoiding debate despite the government's willingness to discuss issues.Yet government business did move, much of it through voice votes amid opposition sloganeering.Eleven Bills were introduced in Lok Sabha and two in Rajya Sabha. Twelve Bills were passed by Lok Sabha and 12 by Rajya Sabha, with 12 Bills cleared by both Houses during the session.Two Bills replacing and incorporating the provisions of ordinances issued before the session, the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 and the Income-Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, were also passed by both Houses.The Demands for Excess Grants for 2022-23 were taken up, with the related Appropriation Bill passed by Lok Sabha on August 4 and returned by Rajya Sabha on August 6. The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was referred to a Joint Committee for examination.Among the more politically significant measures was the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced amid concerns over public examinations and paper leaks.The Bill came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced stringent measures to prevent such incidents in the future, including multiple selfie videos directly addressing students.It provides for speedy investigations and time-bound trials, with investigations to be completed within two months and trials within three months. It also provides for Special Fast Track Courts and Special Public Prosecutors, allows the Centre to constitute Special Task Forces where necessary, enhances penalties and creates a time-bound appellate mechanism before a Division Bench of the High Court.The Bill was passed by both Houses and received presidential assent.Its debate also offered a glimpse of how political parties were trying to speak directly to younger voters. BJP’s younger leaders took the lead in explaining the legislation and the Centre’s position, while the opposition made its own pitch. Both sides adopted Gen Z vocabulary, trading barbs with phrases such as “clock it”, “FOMO” and “delulu”.Other major Bills passed during the session included the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, which seeks to bring Vande Mataram within the ambit of the 1971 Act; the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, which proposes stricter procedures for delayed registration; and the MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, which provides for a national digital platform for voluntary registration and seeks to improve access to finance and resolve delayed-payment disputes faster.The Bankers' Books Evidence Bill expands the definition of bankers' books to cover physical, electronic, digital, virtual and cloud-based records. The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill proposes changing the state’s name from Kerala to Keralam. Other legislation dealt with cooperative development, tribunals and the mining sector.But these measures were not what defined the political atmosphere of the session. That distinction belonged to the protests outside.The Monsoon Session opened against the backdrop of a large student mobilisation at Jantar Mantar over NEET examination irregularities.The protest had been building for weeks. Scientist and activist Sonam Wangchuk had been on a hunger strike for more than 20 days when the Centre intervened and removed him from the protest site.His removal intensified the agitation, with students going ahead with their scheduled “Sansad gherao”. Security personnel, including the Rapid Action Force and Delhi Police, were deployed as the protesters marched towards Parliament.The distance was less than 1.5 km, but the march quickly turned into a major confrontation.Pellet guns, lathi-charge and tear gas were used, with more than 60 people injured and admitted to nearby Lady Hardinge Medical College and Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.The police action immediately became a political issue, with opposition leaders turning their focus towards Union home minister Amit Shah because the security forces involved came under the home ministry’s jurisdiction.The student protests subsequently spread beyond Delhi. The pressure group Cockroach Janta Party’s delegation met PM Modi-led cabinet ministers Jagat Prakash Nadda and Jitendra Singh, after which the situation moved towards normalcy.One of the protesters’ major demands was the removal of Dharmendra Pradhan as education minister.On July 25, Pradhan resigned from the post, making his departure one of the defining political developments of the session.Pradhan’s resignation did not end the political confrontation.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi had not joined the initial Jantar Mantar protest but emerged as a prominent voice in the political battle that followed. His focus shifted from Pradhan to Shah, whom he repeatedly attacked over the police crackdown on students on July 20.“As home minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did? Are the people in plainclothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Youth and students, future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability,” Rahul said.He argued that Shah either directly ordered the use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas, making him “culpable” for the treatment of the protesters, or did not know what the police were doing, making him “incompetent”.“In either case, he has to go,” Rahul said, calling on Prime Minister Narendra Modi to sack the home minister.Rahul also alleged that students were facing threats, including through face recognition and Bajrang Dal. “These are our children and the govt has no business threatening them or beating them. They have not committed any crime. They should not be punished,” he said.He later made the demand for Shah’s removal explicit, saying: “Shah is responsible and we are not going to let him get away with it.”At the AICC headquarters, with Shah’s photograph displayed on a large screen, Rahul accused the home minister of being responsible for the treatment of students and criticised his absence from Lok Sabha, saying it showed that he was “guilty”.Inside Parliament, opposition leaders across parties continued to seek answers from Shah and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The issue contributed to repeated disruptions.The government, meanwhile, maintained that Shah was ready to discuss the student protests.In the final week of the session, Shah offered to address the opposition’s concerns directly.He offered to sit in Parliament from “3pm till 3pm the next day” to hear the opposition and respond to its points. Rahul rejected the offer, saying they “seek answers, not lectures”.Shah’s offer came amid demands that he make a statement in Parliament on the police action during the July 20 march over the NEET paper leak.He later wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla seeking time for a discussion on the student protest and NEET paper leak.“As you are aware, Hon’ble parliamentary affairs minister Shri Kiren Rijiju has agreed, on behalf of the government, to a discussion in Parliament on the student movement concerning the NEET examination, during the meeting of the Business Advisory Committee,” Shah said.He also pointed out that the Lok Sabha had already discussed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill during the session, but opposition MPs had not raised the NEET examination issue during that debate.The exchange captured the central political tension of the session.The government pointed to its legislative response and willingness to debate. The opposition demanded direct answers over the handling of the protests and accountability for the police action.The argument was therefore no longer simply about an examination paper leak. It had become a contest over responsibility, policing and ministerial accountability, much of it fought outside the chamber.Examination irregularities also became a political issue in Jharkhand, where the Centre’s political opponents were in power.Students in the state protested over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, including JPSC and JSSC, under the Hemant Soren government.In Ranchi, protesters marched towards the state assembly in an “assembly gherao”. The Soren government said it was open to talks and held rounds of discussions with student delegations.For the BJP at the Centre, the Jharkhand protests provided an opportunity to counter Rahul Gandhi’s attacks over the student movement in Delhi.Pradhan, days after resigning as education minister, turned his fire on Rahul.“The leader of opposition, who habitually lies, neither wants to come to Parliament nor listen to answers. They just want to spread their lies and shed crocodile tears,” Pradhan said.He also accused Rahul of making “baseless, factless false accusations” against Shah.The political irony was clear: the examination issue that had put the Union government under pressure in Delhi was now being used by the BJP to target the Congress, which is part of the ruling alliance with the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha government led by Hemant Soren.The student protests showed how street mobilisation could shape parliamentary politics. Another demonstration showed how the Parliament complex itself could become a stage for political messaging.The alleged theft of donations at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya became another opposition issue during the session.On Friday, Independent MP Pappu Yadav, along with other opposition MPs, staged a symbolic protest at Makar Dwar over the alleged embezzlement of Ram Temple donations. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party MPs Awadhesh Prasad and Dharmendra Yadav, and Jharkhand Mukti Morcha MP Mahua Maji participated.The MPs held placards and a large banner reading “Amit Shah Sadan Se Gayab Kyun?” They also raised slogans demanding Shah’s resignation and his presence in the House.Pappu Yadav, whose real name is Rajesh Ranjan, dressed as a temple priest carrying a photograph of Lord Ram and sat beside donation boxes. Opposition MPs acted as devotees and placed money in the box. Yadav then symbolically slipped the money into his pocket, representing the opposition’s allegation of theft.Videos circulating online also showed Rahul Gandhi putting money into the donation box. Another MP, playing a devotee, confronted the “priest” over the alleged act.The priest denied wrongdoing before theatrically leaving the scene. The INDIA bloc said the demonstration was intended to highlight the alleged embezzlement of Ram Temple donations and demand accountability from the Centre.It was a symbolic protest, but it reflected the broader character of the session: political messaging increasingly spilled into the physical spaces around Parliament.The Monsoon Session cannot simply be described as one in which Parliament failed to function. Bills were introduced and passed, financial business was completed, ordinances were replaced and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill became law.But the productivity figures tell another story. Lok Sabha functioned for approximately 19% of its scheduled time, while Rajya Sabha functioned for around 39%.Inside the Houses, protests and sloganeering repeatedly led to adjournments. Key government Bills were passed, often through voice votes. Outside, meanwhile, Parliament’s premises became venues for demonstrations and political performances.That contrast defined the session.The Jantar Mantar protest became a parliamentary issue. The police action turned into a political battle over Amit Shah. Pradhan’s resignation followed sustained pressure over the examination controversy. The same issue travelled to Jharkhand, where it became another weapon in the Centre’s political contest with the opposition. The Ram Mandir controversy then produced a symbolic demonstration inside the Parliament complex.In each case, the politics extended beyond the floor of the House.The Monsoon Session thus offered an unusual picture of parliamentary politics: legislation continued inside, while confrontation, mobilisation and political messaging increasingly took place outside. The Houses passed 12 Bills, but some of the session’s most visible battles were fought through protests, slogans, press statements, letters and demonstrations.Parliament was still working. But it was talking less, while the political argument increasingly moved beyond its walls.On August 13, both Houses adjourned sine die and will meet again in the Winter Session.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha functioned for 19% of its scheduled time, Rajya Sabha for around 39%. Question Hour was particularly badly hit, with less than 1% utilised. 12 Bills were passed by Lok Sabha and 12 by Rajya, with 12 Bills cleared by both Houses during the session.

Article Title: Jharkhand students stir: Govt makes fresh peace bid, invites protesters for talks on Aug 17
Article Text:

Six rounds of talks held earlier

NEW DELHI: The Jharkhand government has invited students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations for a fresh round of talks on Monday, August 17, in an attempt to resolve the 23-day-old standoff over demands for a CBI probe and cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination.The talks are scheduled for 2 pm at the State Guest House, with the government also allowing the students to participate alongside their legal advisor, an official said on Sunday.The decision followed a meeting between the Sub-Divisional Officer and the ADM, Law and Order, and protesting students at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where the agitation is being held.“The protesters have been invited for talks on August 17 at 2 pm. The students have been offered the proposal to participate in the discussions along with their legal advisor,” the official said.The ‘JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch’, which is spearheading the agitation, said it had accepted the government's invitation and would attend the meeting, but stressed that its core demands remained unchanged.“We will definitely go for the talks as we want to resolve the issue through dialogue.But, we are firm on two demands – a CBI probe into irregularities in recruitment tests and cancellation of the JSSC-CGL (Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission-Combine Graduate Level) exams,” Manch leader Ravindra Paswan told reporters.Paswan said the talks would be held in the presence of the students' legal advisor. The number of students who will form the delegation to meet the government panel will be announced on Monday.The latest invitation comes after six rounds of discussions between the Jharkhand government and the protesting students failed to produce a settlement.The previous round of talks, held on August 9, ended without any breakthrough.The students have been demanding a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission.They are also seeking cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, one of the key points of contention between the protesters and the state government.The agitation had entered its 23rd day on Sunday, with the students continuing their protest at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.The fresh talks on Monday will therefore be the latest attempt by the government to break the deadlock, with the protesters signalling that they are willing to engage in dialogue but will continue to press for their two principal demands.
Article Summary: The latest invitation comes after six rounds of discussions between the Jharkhand government and the protesting students failed to produce a settlement. NEW DELHI: Police have arrested three persons in connection with the murder of a local Congress leader and his lawyer son in West Bengal’s Nadia district. The investigators have named a jailed man as the alleged mastermind behind the killings, officials said on Sunday.The arrests were made after Anisur Rahman, 50, and his son Abu Sufian, 24, were shot at and attacked with sharp-edged weapons while returning home. The duo was in their car near Nagadi railway gate in Nakashipara when the assault happened around 9.30pm on Saturday. The spot was about 200 metres from their residence.The three accused, identified as Haranagar gram panchayat pradhan Fatima Biwi, Sageb Sk and Mithu Sheikh, were produced before Krishnanagar court and remanded to nine days in police custody.Fatima Biwi’s husband, Jabbar Sheikh, who is currently in jail, has been named as the alleged mastermind. Police, however, said the investigation was still underway and that the exact number of attackers and rounds fired had not yet been established.According to police, Rahman and his son were travelling home when their vehicle was intercepted near the railway gate. The assailants allegedly opened fire at the car before attacking the two men with sharp-edged weapons.Both victims died at the spot due to excessive blood loss.Sufian was a lawyer practising at the Krishnanagar court, while his father was a local Congress leader.Additional Superintendent of Police Surajit Kumar Dey said investigators were working to establish the full sequence of events and identify all those involved.The killings have triggered allegations of political involvement, with Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari alleging that Trinamool Congress operatives were behind the attack.Adhikari said police had informed him that Jabbar Sheikh was the alleged mastermind."The SP informed me that Jabbar Sheikh, who is in jail, is responsible for the murder. His wife, who is a Trinamool panchayat pradhan, has also been arrested. Trinamool operatives committed the murder. The rule of law applies to everyone," Adhikari said.Congress leader Tipu Sultan also alleged that Jabbar Sheikh had orchestrated the killings from jail."Jabbar orchestrated this from jail using miscreants to gain control of the area. If the administration conducts a proper and impartial investigation, everything will become crystal clear," he said.The allegations have not yet been established by the police investigation.Former Congress MP Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury condemned the killings in a social media post, raising concerns over security and political freedom."Such an atrocious incident on Independence Day raises serious questions regarding public security and political freedom," he said.West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar observed a Black Day in protest against the killings and alleged that the attack was pre-planned and politically motivated."A number of panchayat functionaries in Nadia wanted to join Congress and had contacted Anisur Rahman for that purpose. BJP did not want that to happen," he alleged.Police are continuing their investigation to determine the motive, establish the number of people involved in the attack and ascertain the precise circumstances leading to the double murder.
Article Summary: Anisur Rahman, 50, and his son Abu Sufian, 24, were shot at and attacked with sharp-edged weapons while returning home. The three accused, identified as Haranagar gram panchayat pradhan Fatima Biwi, Sageb Sk and Mithu Sheikh, were produced before Krishnanagar court and remanded to nine days in police custody.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has demanded Bombay HC clerk recruitment exam to be conducted afresh after alleged technical glitches triggered concerns among candidates.While talking to reports, Dipke said candidates informed him that several computers developed problems soon after they began the test, with some reporting non-functional mice while others faced faulty keyboards."Students just informed me that they had a High Court exam this morning. Article Title: Centre orders corrective measures after CAG flags unsafe drinking water at railway stations
Article Text:
